main_theorem: Let d>=4 be even, k>=2 an integer, and J_0 any skew-symmetric unitary. Every k-positive map Phi(Z)=a Tr(Z)I_d+bZ+c J_0 Z^T J_0^*, with real a,b,c, has decomposable Choi compression to every input or output subspace of dimension at most min(2k,d). Equivalently, its Choi expectation on every PPT source stays nonnegative after arbitrary local filters A,B whenever rank(A)<=min(2k,d) OR rank(B)<=min(2k,d). If k>=d/2 the entire map is decomposable. Finite sums of arbitrary local completely-positive images of such witnesses and of decomposable witnesses inherit the filter property. In particular, for k=2 no such map or CP-generated sum can supply a rank<=4 negative filter for ANY PPT source. The family contains indecomposable examples when d>2k. This is a map-cone obstruction, not a global 4x4 PPT/SN3 conclusion.
normalization_and_exact_choi_orientation: For nonzero positive Phi, s=ad+b+c>0 because Phi(I)=sI and a positive map vanishing at I is zero. Divide by s and put t=a/s, p=b/s, q=c/s, so dt+p+q=1 and Phi_(p,q)(Z)=t Tr(Z)I+pZ+qJ_0 Z^T J_0^*. Its unnormalized Choi matrix is C=t I+p[Omega]+q(I tensor J_0)F(I tensor J_0^*), where Omega=sum_i|ii>. Conjugating by the local unitary I tensor J_0^* gives C_hat=t I+p[j]+qF with K_0=conjugate(J_0) and j=(I tensor J_0^*)Omega=vec(K_0). The rotated K_0, not J_0, is the skew form used in every subsequent vector, canonicalization and source calculation; it is skew-unitary, Fj=-j, and ||j||^2=d. The Park BH_l point p=-1/(ld-l-1), q=-l/(ld-l-1) has t=l/(ld-l-1), so C_hat=(lI-lF-[j])/(ld-l-1), an exact unnormalized Choi/local-unitary match. Local unitaries preserve decomposability and filter ranks.
four_necessary_tests_all_parities: Set l=min(k,d/2)>=2 and r=2 floor(l/2). A k-positive map is l-positive. In a standard symplectic basis of K_0, for a unit vector x of Schmidt rank <=l write f=<x|F|x> and h=|<j|x>|^2. Four available tests are: (i) |e_1,e_1> with (f,h)=(1,0); (ii) (|e_1,e_2>-|e_2,e_1>)/sqrt(2), with e_1,e_2 in a symplectic isotropic subspace, gives (-1,0); (iii) the normalized sum over r/2 full symplectic pairs (|e_i,f_i>-|f_i,e_i>)/sqrt(r) gives (-1,r); (iv) the normalized sum over l distinct symplectic pairs |e_i,f_i>/sqrt(l) gives (0,l). These exist for every parity since 2l<=d. They imply the necessary inequalities u=t+q>=0, v=t-q>=0, w=t-q+rp>=0, x=t+lp>=0.
quadrilateral_enclosure: With dt+p+q=1, these halfplanes form a bounded quadrilateral with vertices A=(1,0), B=(0,1/(d+1)), C=(-1/D,(l-r)/D) for D=ld+l-r-1, and D_BH=(-1/E,-l/E) for E=ld-l-1. Consecutive equalities u=v, v=w, w=x, x=u give these four vertices. The remaining pairwise intersections violate x>=0 or w>=0; boundedness follows from t>=|q| and x>=0. At A the map is CP; at B the rotated Choi is (I+F)/(d+1)>=0. At C the ORIGINAL-basis map is [l Tr(Z)I-Z+(l-r)J_0 Z^T J_0^*]/D, which is completely copositive: the Choi partial transpose of l Tr(Z)I-Z is lI-F>=0, and the last term is also co-CP. At D_BH the map is the l-Breuer-Hall map. Thus any l-positive map in the family is a convex combination of three globally decomposable vertices and BH_l. When l is even this quadrilateral is the exact l-positivity region because all four vertices are l-positive; when l is odd it is only a necessary enclosure, and no equality with the actual generally curved region is claimed.
bh_positivity: For a coefficient matrix Y of rank <=l let S=(Y-Y^T)/2. Then rank(S)<=2l and |Tr(K_0^*S)|^2<=||S||_*^2<=2l||S||_F^2. Consequently <Y|(lI-lF-[j])|Y>=2l||S||_F^2-|Tr(K_0^*S)|^2>=0. Hence BH_l itself is l-positive, and if d>2l its indecomposability follows from the PPT pairing below.
bh_compression_canonical_form: For any 2l-dimensional isometry U, write E=ran(U), choose a complement U_perp, and let G=U^*K_0 conjugate(U), N=U^*K_0 conjugate(U_perp). The standard complex skew-unitary-congruence normal form gives G=direct_sum_i lambda_i[[0,1],[-1,0]], 0<=lambda_i<=1. Since GG^*+NN^*=I, put s_i=sqrt(1-lambda_i^2); the nonzero row pairs of N are mutually orthogonal and can be aligned with distinct pairs p_i,q_i of output-complement coordinates. After these local basis choices, j_U=(U^* tensor I)j=sum_i lambda_i a_i+sum_(s_i>0)s_i c_i, with a_i=|2i-1,2i>-|2i,2i-1> and c_i=|2i-1,p_i>-|2i,q_i>. These mutually orthogonal vectors have squared norm 2, and sum lambda_i^2+sum s_i^2=l. The compressed Choi matrix is C_U=l I-lF_E-[j_U], where F_E is swap on the input/output E block and zero on the output complement. The skew-unitary congruence theorem is a named standard linear-algebra import.
bh_compression_psd_plus_copositive: For each defective pair set h_i=|2i-1,q_i>+|2i,p_i>. Let u_alpha list the a_i and defective c_i and w_alpha their respective lambda_i and s_i. Let A_other contain unnormalized antisymmetric |p,q>-|q,p> in the input/E block except the l paired a_i, and B_other the standard |p,o> with output o outside E except the 2x2 input/output block of each defective pair. Then C_U=P+l sum_(s_i>0)[h_i]^Gamma_in, where P=sum_(alpha<beta)[w_alpha u_beta-w_beta u_alpha]+l sum_(v in A_other)[v]+l sum_(v in B_other)[v] is explicitly PSD. Indeed lI-lF_E equals 2l on the antisymmetric E sector, 0 on the symmetric E sector and l outside E. Each [h_i]^Gamma has eigenvalue -1 on c_i, +1 on its symmetric companion and on the two cross basis vectors in that defective 2x2 block. The remaining span of the normalized u_alpha has diagonal 2l, while [j_U] is 2ww^T with ||w||^2=l; the first PSD sum equals 2(lI-ww^T). All other PSD terms are exactly as displayed. Smaller input ranks follow by isometric extension and completely-positive precomposition. Since C_hat=tI+p[j]+qF is swap invariant, the same conclusion holds for output compression.
all_sources_and_cp_closure: A Hermitian witness C has no rank<=r input-filter negative pairing on any PPT source iff every r-dimensional input compression is decomposable: use the duality between the PPT cone and P+Q^Gamma with P,Q>=0, and preservation of PPT under local CP filtering. The decomposable cone is closed because the traces of PSD P,Q are nonnegative and sum to the trace of P+Q^Gamma. Intersections of these compression cones are closed and convex. Local CP images preserve the property: after a rank<=r filter, each Kraus summand has an effective filter of rank <=r, and decomposable compressed witnesses remain decomposable under the other local CP map. Sums and added decomposable witnesses preserve it. The generated maps remain k-positive when all added terms are themselves k-positive; the no-PPT-pairing statement does not require that extra hypothesis.
nontriviality_and_scope: For d>2k, take the ROTATED-form source R=I+F+[j], with j=vec(K_0). It is PSD because I+F>=0, and R^Gamma=I+[Omega]+(I tensor conjugate(K_0))F(I tensor conjugate(K_0)^*) is PSD because the twisted swap is a Hermitian involution. Tr[(kI-kF-[j])R]=d(2k-d)<0, so BH_k is indecomposable. Mixing its normalized point with the identity map by weight lambda in 0<=lambda<(d-2k)/(d-2k+d(kd-k-1)) retains negative pairing with R while every rank<=2k compression is decomposable; for d=6,k=2 the interval is 0<=lambda<1/28. The original 4x4 PPT/SN3 target remains OPEN; no general nonexistence is claimed.
